title.value: Molecular Geometry Pretraining with SE(3)-Invariant Denoising Distance Matching
title.justification: The paper introduces a novel approach to pretrain molecular geometries by denoising distance matching while ensuring SE(3) invariance. This title captures the essence of the entire work.
title.quote: Molecular representation pretraining is critical in various applications for drug and material discovery due to the limited number of labeled molecules, and most existing work focuses on pretraining on 2D molecular graphs.

extractions.description: The paper presents a new method called GeoSSL-DDM to pretrain molecular geometries using SE(3)-Invariant denoising, which focuses on denoising pairwise atomic distances in molecules. This approach is designed to improve the robustness of molecular representations by learning from 3D geometric structures rather than the traditional 2D topological approach. The method promises advancements in drug and material discovery by offering more effective pretraining on unlabeled molecular data.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily discusses computational advancements in molecular geometry representation, which indirectly may influence sustainable applications but does not directly focus on climate or ecological sustainable development.

primary_category.quote: The main challenge for molecule geometric pretraining arises from discovering an effective proxy task to empower the pretraining to extract essential features from the 3D geometric structures.

secondary_categories.justification: Although the methods discussed can be applied to material discovery, the paper does not specifically link its findings to climate or ecological sustainable development.
